why: The MCP capabilities an Overnight Agent run depends on, declared ONCE (GH #346).
Before this file existed the list was implied by prose scattered through SKILL.md,
which meant nothing could probe it: a capability the run silently lacked produced no
error at the point of use, because an absent tool is not a failing tool. The email row
is the load-bearing one -- PHASE 0 mandates an inbox read, and an unhealthy email client
answers a search with [], which is byte-identical to a genuinely empty inbox.
Read by check-agent-inbox.ps1. Add a row here rather than a sentence in SKILL.md.

capabilities.why: PHASE 0 reads the agent inbox for emailed instructions. Emptiness may only be reported after a POSITIVE health probe: a dropped instruction email is invisible and unrecoverable, so this fails closed and loud.
notes: healthField is 'success' from email_test_account and NOT 'connected' from
email_list_accounts. Measured 2026-09-02 12:52 PT: the account reported
"connected": false while email_test_account returned
{"success":true,"folderCount":10} against the same live server. The field an agent
would naturally read is not the field that reflects reality, so the verdict is taken
from a call that does work, never from an advertised flag.

capabilities.why: The mirror surfaces the run to the phone. Its absence degrades reach but does not drop an input channel, so it is reported rather than raised as an ask.

PHASE 0.7 reads the catch-up doc comments, which Shiv designated the PRIMARY communication mechanism. doc_new_comments comes from the last -Observe and never calls Google, so a run whose server is dead reports '0 new comments' -- byte-identical to a document he has not commented on. That is the #346 defect on its third surface, and on the channel he was told to prefer over email.
notes: mandatory:true is a judgement call, and #459 left it explicitly open. Taken because
(a) it is his stated primary channel, so a silent loss is at least as bad as a lost
inbox, which is exactly what mandatory exists for; (b) the alarm-fatigue argument is
weak for THIS probe kind -- mcp-tools only enumerates tools, so it fires when the
server cannot start at all, not on a transient Google API error; (c) reverting is one
character. Flip it to false if it proves noisy.
Measured 2026-09-04: `node mcp-probe.mjs google-workspace list` exited 0 with 36 tools,
both list_document_comments and get_doc_content present -- so this ships GREEN on a
healthy server rather than as a permanently-red check. Discrimination measured the
other way too: an unreachable server name yields verdict=unavailable/mcp-unavailable,
and requiring a tool the server does not expose yields missing-tools, both exit 2.
SCOPE -- READ THIS BEFORE TREATING A GREEN ROW AS 'THE DOC CHANNEL IS UP'. This row
does NOT detect the mode-B mid-run death that motivated #459, and that was measured,
not reasoned: at 01:2x PT on 2026-09-04 the agent session's google-workspace server
returned 'Transport closed' on two consecutive calls and never recovered, while this
probe -- run in the same minute -- exited 0 with all 36 tools present. mcp-probe.mjs
SPAWNS A FRESH SERVER from mcp-config.json, so it answers 'can a server be started?',
never 'is the connection my session is using still alive?'. Its own header says so:
'a probe that passes on connection A says nothing about connection B'. The email row
escapes this because the run READS the inbox through the probe, so probe-session and
work-session are the same one; PHASE 0.7 reads doc comments through the agent's own
MCP tools, so they are not. What this row does cover is real and worth having: a
server that cannot start, is absent from mcp-config.json, fails its handshake, or has
renamed/dropped a required tool. What it does not cover is tracked separately.

capabilities.why: The google-workspace row above proves the SERVER is reachable. It cannot prove the server can reach GOOGLE, because tools/list needs no authorization -- measured 2026-09-04, the server enumerates all 36 tools regardless of credential state. This row tests the refresh token itself, which is the half that actually fails: a testing-mode OAuth refresh token expires about every 7 days and silently breaks every Google Workspace tool until Shiv re-consents. Without it the doc channel's probe would be green through the entire outage window.
notes: Exit codes are check-google-token.ps1's own documented contract: 0=ok, 2=expired
(re-auth needed), 3=transient error, 4=credential file missing. 3 is deliberately in
NEITHER list -- it maps to `inconclusive`, which is reported but does not raise the ask,
because a check that cries wolf on a flaky network is a check nobody reads.
Measured 2026-09-04: exit 0, status=ok, 'Refresh token valid; Google issued a fresh
access token', so this ships green. Discrimination measured by pointing the row at a
missing script (script-missing) and by a non-zero declared exit (probe-failed), both
verdict=unavailable and both taking the run to exit 2.
The credential store is single-user and holds shiv@bijlanis.com. Calling a Google tool
with a DIFFERENT address does not fall back -- it starts an interactive OAuth flow and
wedges the server for the rest of the session ('Transport closed' on every later call).
That was observed live on 2026-09-04 and is worth knowing before debugging a 'dead'
Google server: check the address before concluding the server died.

capabilities.why: Browser slot health has its own, much deeper probe (a bounded CDP work probe, GH #197). Listing it here without probing it would be a second, weaker opinion about the same subsystem, so this row names the owner instead of duplicating it.
